mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6% in one month (vs previous month)
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which compresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the average return is not statistically below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months indicates a broad-based weakening in demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is cut by at least 0.5 percentage points within a quarter, liquidity conditions ease, lowering risk premia and boosting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls by >= 0.5% within a quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered quarters, or the average return is not statistically above zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) in the same month (due to large labor force entrants) signals a mismatch in the labor market, which increases uncertainty and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such months, or the median return is not statistically below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the average return is not statistically above zero at the 5% level.
